transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Lately I just can’t think straight or make decisions at work the way I used to. My primary doctor referred me to you after a colleague at the distribution center pointed out that my leadership has been kind of unpredictable lately. I'm just trying to figure out what's going on.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, such as feeling sad, empty, or irritable, that might be contributing to your difficulties with decision-making and leadership at work?

Yes, my mood has been swinging back and forth, and it's really messing with my work. Lately, I've been in this heavy slump where my head feels like mud, I second-guess every decision, and I feel like a total failure as a boss. But before this, I had these wired periods where I'd get so snappy and irritable that I'd bark at my team over the smallest things.
Can you tell me more about these 'wired periods' you mentioned, like how often they happen and what you do during those times?

These "high gear" periods have been happening off and on for a couple of years, but they really ramped up over this past year. When they hit, my mind races, I feel like I can run the whole company, and I'll stay up until 2 a.m. working on my motorcycle or taking on extra projects at work. I even end up putting big charges on my credit card for tools without talking to my wife because I feel so unstoppable.
Can you estimate how long these 'wired periods' typically last, and how often do you experience them in a given month?

I’m not really sure about the exact number of times they happen a month, but those "on weeks" usually seem to last for a week or so at a time. They've just been coming and going off and on like that over the last couple of years, so it's hard to give a precise count.

Can you describe how these episodes of feeling 'wired' and the episodes of feeling down or 'in a slump' relate to each other in terms of timing, do they switch back and forth or do you experience long periods of one before switching to the other?

They've been alternating back and forth off and on for at least the past couple of years. This current slump has been dragging on for a really long time, since around last fall, though I did have a brief, wired high period for a few weeks right before it hit.
Can you clarify if these periods of feeling 'wired' and being in a 'slump' have been happening within the same month, or are they more spaced out, occurring in different months?

They can actually happen pretty close together, sometimes even within the same month. For instance, I had one of those wired, snappy periods just a few weeks before this current long slump started last fall. These alternating stretches of being in "high gear" and then "slumping" have been going off and on like this for the past couple of years.

To help clarify your condition, can you tell me if you've experienced any periods of at least two weeks where you felt consistently depressed, without any of the 'wired' episodes, or have the 'wired' and 'slump' periods always alternated?

While they used to alternate, this current slump has been completely different. I've been consistently down and exhausted since last fall—almost a year now—without any of those wired or high periods at all. It's just been a heavy, non-stop low that I can't seem to shake.
During this current long slump that's lasted almost a year, have you experienced any significant loss of interest in activities you once enjoyed, or changes in appetite or sleep patterns?

Yes, since last fall I’ve completely lost interest in my hobbies, to the point where I just stare at my motorcycle tools or fishing rod and end up sitting on the couch doing nothing. My appetite has also disappeared, and I have to remind myself to eat because I'll get home at night and realize all I've had is a cup of coffee and maybe a leftover sandwich.
Have you been experiencing feelings of guilt or worthlessness during this long slump that's lasted almost a year?

Yes, very much so. When I make a minor mistake like messing up a schedule or forgetting to sign off on a report, I don't just feel bad—I feel like a complete failure as a boss, a husband, and a father. I start thinking that everyone would be better off if they hadn't counted on me in the first place.

During either your 'wired' periods or your current long slump, have you ever experienced any unusual perceptions, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others cannot, or had beliefs that seem unreal to others?
No, I've never experienced anything like that during either my high or low periods. I have never heard voices, seen things that aren't there, or had any unusual beliefs that others found strange.

Can you confirm if your current long slump, which has lasted almost a year, is the longest period you've experienced without any 'wired' episodes, and if so, does this seem different from the pattern of alternating episodes you described earlier?

Yes, this is definitely the longest I've ever gone without one of those "wired" periods. Usually, the high and low phases would switch back and forth every few weeks or months over the past couple of years. This slump has just been dragging on since last fall, and it feels much heavier and completely different from my usual pattern.

Given that your current slump has lasted almost a year without any 'wired' episodes, and considering your history of alternating between 'wired' and 'slump' periods, do you think this prolonged slump might be a significant departure from your usual pattern of mood swings?

Yes, it really is a huge departure from my usual pattern. While I've had those ups and downs off and on for a couple of years, this slump has dragged on since last fall without any "wired" periods to break it up, making it feel much heavier and more prolonged than before.
Can you specify the exact number of months you've been experiencing this current long slump without any 'wired' episodes, to help clarify if it meets the criteria for a persistent depressive episode?

It started around last fall, so it's been about ten or eleven months of feeling this way. It's been weighing me down for most of this past year, without a single moment of that wired energy. It just feels like a constant, heavy fog that won't lift.

You've mentioned that this current slump has lasted about ten or eleven months without any 'wired' episodes, which is different from your previous pattern of alternating episodes. Can you confirm if, during the past couple of years, you've had any periods where you were not experiencing either a 'wired' episode or a 'slump', essentially periods of normal mood in between these episodes?

Yes, because those stretches of feeling low and revved up were "off and on" over the past couple of years, I did have times in between where my mood leveled out and I felt like my normal self. This past year has really just been dominated by this continuous low slump, but before that, I definitely had those steady periods in between the swings.

Considering your history of mood swings and this current long slump, do you think the absence of 'wired' episodes during the past ten or eleven months indicates a shift towards a more persistent depressive state, or do you believe your condition is still characterized by the potential for future 'wired' episodes?

I'm really not sure what this means for the future or if my mood has permanently shifted. All I know is that I've been stuck in this heavy low since last fall, and I feel too exhausted to really know what to expect next.

I believe it's all part of the same pattern of ups and downs I've had over the last couple of years, rather than a separate issue. Even though this current slump has dragged on much longer since last fall and feels heavier, it still feels like a continuation of those alternating "high gear" and "slump" cycles. In fact, my primary doctor also noticed this longstanding pattern of mood and energy shifts, which is why he referred me here.
